questions.story: 2031 and 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup bids
questions.question: Where is the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup set to take place after being awarded to a four-nation joint bid?
options: Japan, South Korea, China, and Taiwan
Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico, and the United States
Australia, New Zealand, Fiji, and Samoa
questions.explanation: FIFA confirmed the North and Central American joint bid from Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico, and the US for the 2031 tournament.
questions.context: 2031 and 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup bids: In association football, FIFA confirms Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico, and the United States as joint hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, while England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales will jointly host the 2035 tournament.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of Spain granted an amnesty to which former regional leader living in self-imposed exile in Belgium?
questions.explanation: Spanish judges granted an amnesty to former Catalan leader Carles Puigdemont, concluding legal proceedings related to the 2017 independence declaration.
questions.context: 2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis: The Supreme Court of Spain grants amnesty to former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont, who is currently in self-imposed exile in Belgium, thereby bringing the legal proceedings against the leaders of the October 2017 declaration of independence to a definitive close.

questions.story: Myanmar–United Kingdom relations, Rohingya genocide case
questions.question: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband recently announced sanctions against military figures from which nation, while formally recognising the Rohingya genocide?
questions.explanation: The British government targetted five military figures in Myanmar with new sanctions and officially recognised the Rohingya genocide.
questions.context: Myanmar–United Kingdom relations, Rohingya genocide case: British foreign secretary Ed Miliband announces sanctions against five military leaders of Myanmar, while also granting recognition of the Rohingya genocide.

questions.question: According to Turkish intelligence, the Kurdistan Workers' Party has begun pulling out of additional bases in which country as part of a disarmament agreement?
questions.explanation: Disarmament steps saw the Kurdistan Workers' Party abandon 14 positions in northern Iraq.
questions.context: Kurdish–Turkish conflict: Turkish intelligence reports that the Kurdistan Workers' Party withdraws from 14 additional bases in northern Iraq as part of an ongoing disarmament process aimed at ending its conflict with Turkey.

questions.question: Schools in Germany and which neighbouring Scandinavian country were targeted by widespread bomb threats via email?
questions.explanation: Hundreds of academic institutions across Denmark and Germany were sent automated threat messages, though police advised them to stay open.
questions.context: 2026 European bomb threat wave: Hundreds of schools across Denmark and Germany receive bomb threats via email, with police ordering the schools to continue operations as normal.
